learn.hook: Nani Maa hides some seeds under her hand. She shows the rest. Can you tell how many are hiding?
points: If we know the total and can see some, the hidden ones = total − the ones we can see.
10 seeds, 6 can be seen: 10 − 6 = 4 are hidden.
A table helps: total, seen, hidden. Totals can go up to about 27.
Know your number pairs by heart: pairs that make 9 (4 + 5), 10 (3 + 7) and 20 (12 + 8).

example.q: Nani Maa has 20 seeds. You can see 13. How many are hidden?

learn.reallife: When some sweets in a box of 20 are eaten, the empty spaces tell you how many are gone.

quiz.q: Nani Maa has 10 seeds. She hides some and you see 3. How many are hidden?
quiz.mistake: Adds the seen seeds to the total

quiz.q: There are 9 seeds. 4 are showing. How many are under her hand?
quiz.mistake: Thinks the hidden part equals the seen part

quiz.q: Total 20 seeds, 11 can be seen. How many are hidden?
Total 27 seeds, 18 can be seen. How many are hidden?
Which pair makes 20?
quiz.mistake: Makes only the ones add to 10 without checking tens

quiz.q: Which pair does NOT make 9?
Nani Maa shows 16 seeds and says 'There are 24 in all.' How many is she hiding?
6 + ___ = 10. What is the missing number?

teach.ask: Gappu had 15 seeds. His friend hid some and Gappu can see 9. How does he find the hidden ones?
teach.praise: 15 take away 9 is 6 hidden seeds! Chirp!
teach.nudge: What do I do with the total and the seeds I can see?

learn.hook: A tens frame has 10 boxes. When it is full, you have made a ten!
points: For small sums, draw dots for each number and count all the dots.
A tens frame has 2 rows of 5 boxes. A full frame is 10.
To add 6 + 8: put 6 dots, then fill the frame with 4 more from the 8. 10 and 4 left = 14.
To take away 18 − 9: one full frame and 8 more. Take 8 from the extra, then 1 from the full frame. 9 are left.

steps: Move 3 of the 5 to fill the frame: 10.

learn.reallife: Egg trays and laddoo boxes often hold 10 or 12, so you can quickly see how many are missing.

quiz.q: 6 + 8 using a tens frame. How many are left over after the frame is full?
quiz.explain: 6 + 4 fills the frame. 8 − 4 = 4 left over. So 6 + 8 = 14.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the leftover is the second number

quiz.q: What is 6 + 8?
quiz.mistake: Writes the digits side by side

quiz.q: What is 18 − 9?
quiz.explain: 18 is 10 and 8. Take 8, then 1 more from the 10. 9 are left.

quiz.q: Riya draws 4 dots and 3 dots. How many dots in all?
A full tens frame and 3 more dots show which number?
To add 9 + 5 with a tens frame, how many of the 5 do you move to fill the frame?
Nani Maa had 15 balushahis. The children ate 7. How many are left?
Which tens frame trick gives 7 + 6?
quiz.explain: 7 + 3 makes 10, and 3 of the 6 are left: 10 + 3 = 13.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to take the moved dots away

teach.ask: Gappu wants to add 8 + 7 with a tens frame. How should he do it?
teach.praise: 8 + 2 fills the frame, 5 left over, so 15! Chirp!
teach.nudge: How many of the 7 do I need to fill the frame?

learn.hook: Riya is going to Nani Maa's village by train! Let's add up all the fun things on the trip.
points: Adding means putting things together to find the total.
Words like 'in all', 'altogether' and 'total' tell us to add.
Add the tens, then the ones: for 34 + 25, do 30 + 20 = 50 and 4 + 5 = 9. So 34 + 25 = 59.
If the ones make 10 or more, they make a new ten. Add it to the tens.

example.q: Nani Maa picked 26 mangoes on Monday and 18 mangoes on Tuesday. How many mangoes in all?

learn.reallife: On a trip we add up tickets, snacks and even the cows we spot from the train window!

items.text: Riya had 12 shells and found ___ more. Now she has 20.

quiz.q: From the train window, Arjun counted 34 cows and then 23 goats. How many animals did he count in all?
Nani Maa made 45 laddoos and 28 jalebis. How many sweets did she make altogether?
quiz.mistake: Forgets the new ten made by 5 + 8 = 13

quiz.q: Riya's train ticket cost ₹65 and her brother's ticket also cost ₹65. What was the total cost?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to add the 10 made by 5 + 5

quiz.q: At Nani Maa's farm there are 16 hens and 7 ducks. How many birds are there in all?
quiz.mistake: Counts on but misses one step

quiz.q: Which words in a story tell you to ADD?
quiz.explain: 'In all' means put everything together, so we add. The others mean something was taken away.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up adding words with taking-away words

quiz.q: Meena walked 38 steps to the well and 38 steps back. How many steps did she walk?
quiz.mistake: Forgets the new ten made by 8 + 8 = 16

quiz.q: Joseph has 50 marbles. Nani Maa gives him 25 more. How many marbles does he have now?
quiz.explain: He gets more, so we add. 50 + 25 = 75.
quiz.mistake: Takes away when the story says he got more

quiz.q: Riya packed 14 frocks, 6 T-shirts and 10 pairs of socks. How many things did she pack?
quiz.mistake: Adds only two of the three groups

teach.ask: Gappu has 25 berries and finds 13 more. He wants to know how many he has now. How should he work it out?
teach.praise: Tens with tens, ones with ones! I have 38 berries. Yum!
teach.nudge: Should I add or take away? And which parts do I add first?

learn.hook: Nani Maa had a big basket of mangoes, but the monkeys came visiting! How many are left?
points: Subtracting means taking away to find what is left.
Words like 'left', 'gave away', 'how many more' and 'difference' tell us to subtract.
Take away tens, then ones: for 58 − 23, do 50 − 20 = 30 and 8 − 3 = 5. So 58 − 23 = 35.
If there are not enough ones, break a ten into 10 ones.
Check by adding back: 35 + 23 = 58.

example.q: Nani Maa had 52 mangoes. The monkeys took 17. How many mangoes are left?

learn.reallife: When you spend some of your pocket money at the village fair, subtraction tells you how much is left.

games.title: True or false?
items: 4 tens − 2 tens = 2 tens, and the 8 ones stay. That is 28.
Taking away makes a number smaller. 60 − 5 = 55.
Take everything away and nothing is left.
'How many are left?' tells us to add.
'Left' means some were taken away, so we subtract.

quiz.q: Arjun took 40 photos on the trip. He deleted 15 blurry ones. How many photos are left?
The train coach had 86 seats. 54 people sat down. How many seats are empty?
quiz.explain: Take the filled seats away from all the seats: 86 − 54 = 32.

quiz.q: Nani Maa had 30 cups of milk. She used 12 cups to make kheer. How many cups are left?
quiz.explain: 30 − 12: take away 10 to get 20, then take away 2 more to get 18.
quiz.mistake: Does 2 − 0 instead of 0 − 2 in the ones place and gets 22

quiz.q: Kabir is 9 years old and Nani Maa is 64 years old. How much older is Nani Maa?
quiz.explain: 'How much older' asks for the difference. 64 − 9 = 55.
quiz.mistake: Adds the two ages instead of finding the difference

quiz.q: Riya has 25 bangles. She wants 40 bangles for a wedding. How many more bangles does she need?
quiz.explain: Count on from 25 to 40: that is 15. So 40 − 25 = 15.
quiz.mistake: Adds 25 and 40 instead of finding what is missing

quiz.q: Meena had ₹70. She bought a kite for ₹35. How much money does she have left?
quiz.explain: 70 − 35: take away 30 to get 40, then take away 5 to get 35.
quiz.mistake: Adds the price instead of taking it away

quiz.q: Which addition checks that 62 − 27 = 35 is correct?
quiz.explain: Add the answer to the number taken away. If you get back 62, the subtraction is right. 35 + 27 = 62.
quiz.mistake: Adds the two numbers from the question instead of the answer and the number taken away

quiz.q: There were 48 chickens in the yard. 19 went into the coop. How many are still outside?
quiz.explain: 48 − 19: take away 10 to get 38, then take away 9 to get 29.
quiz.mistake: Takes the smaller ones digit from the bigger one (9 − 8 = 1) and gets 31

teach.ask: Gappu had 32 seeds and ate 15. He wants to know how many are left but doesn't know where to start. Help him!
teach.praise: I break a ten when I need more ones! I have 17 seeds left. Chirp!
teach.nudge: But 2 is smaller than 5. What can I do with the ones?

learn.hook: 2, 4 and 6 are a family! Can you make 4 number facts with them?
points: Three numbers can make an addition and a subtraction fact: 2 + 4 = 6 and 6 − 4 = 2.
The biggest number is the total. The two smaller ones are the parts.
One family gives 4 facts: 2 + 4 = 6, 4 + 2 = 6, 6 − 2 = 4, 6 − 4 = 2.
Addition and subtraction are related: if you know one, you know the others.
Not every three numbers make a family: 2, 3 and 7 do not, because 2 + 3 is 5.

example.q: Make the four facts for 5, 8 and 13.

learn.reallife: If you know 7 + 8 = 15, you also know 15 − 8 = 7. Shopkeepers use such facts to give change quickly.

quiz.q: Which three cards make a number fact?
quiz.mistake: Picks numbers that are close together

quiz.q: 8 + 5 = 13. Which fact is in the same family?
quiz.explain: Take one part from the total and you get the other part.
quiz.mistake: Adds the total to a part

quiz.q: If 6 + 9 = 15, what is 15 − 9?
quiz.mistake: Gives the part that was taken away

quiz.q: How many facts can we write with 2, 7 and 9?
Which numbers do NOT make a family?
quiz.mistake: Checks only that one number is biggest

quiz.q: In the family 7, 8 and 15, which number is the total?
quiz.explain: The biggest number is the total. 7 + 8 = 15.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the first number is the total

quiz.q: Find the missing number to make a family: 4, ___, 11
Arun knows 9 + 4 = 13. How does that help him with 13 − 4?
quiz.mistake: Thinks addition and subtraction are unrelated

teach.ask: Gappu has cards 3, 6 and 9. How can he make four facts with them?
teach.nudge: What subtraction facts can I make from 3 + 6 = 9?

learn.hook: Ravi has 22 stamps and wants 52. How many more does he need?
points: A missing-part sentence looks like 22 + ___ = 52.
To find the missing part, take the part you know from the total: 52 − 22 = 30.
52 stamps, 37 are Indian: 52 − 37 = 15 are from other countries.
On a number line, jump from the smaller number to the total. Add up the jumps: 37 → 40 is 3, 40 → 52 is 12, so 15.
learn.reallife: Collectors count how many more stamps or cards they need to finish an album.

games.title: Missing part facts
items: We can count on with jumps to find a missing part.
Jump from the part to the total.

quiz.q: 22 + ___ = 52. What is the missing number?
Sunil has 52 stamps. 37 are from India. How many are from other countries?
quiz.mistake: Takes the smaller digit from the bigger in each place

quiz.q: Leela has 46 stamps. She wants 60. How many more does she need?
quiz.mistake: Forgets the small jump to the next ten

quiz.q: ___ + 25 = 70. What is the missing number?
On a number line, Raju jumps from 28 to 30, then to 50. How much did he add in all?
Which sentence finds the missing part in 33 + ___ = 81?
quiz.explain: Total minus the known part gives the missing part.
quiz.mistake: Adds the total and the part

quiz.q: A stamp album holds 90 stamps. 64 are filled. How many empty places?
Kiran says 52 − 37 = 25. Check by adding back. Is he right?
quiz.explain: 37 + 25 = 62, not 52. The right answer is 15, since 37 + 15 = 52.
quiz.mistake: Does not check by adding back

teach.ask: Gappu has 27 feathers and wants 40. How can he find how many more he needs?
teach.praise: 27 to 30 is 3, 30 to 40 is 10, so 13 more! Chirp!
teach.nudge: How can I jump from 27 to 40 on a number line?

topics.title: Bead string and jumps of ten

learn.hook: 7, 17, 27, 37... What do you notice about the ones digit?
points: A bead string (ginladi) has beads in groups of 10, so we can add and take away quickly.
34 + 6: from 34, move 6 beads to reach the next ten, 40.
42 − 15: from 42, take away 10 to get 32, then 5 more to get 27.
Jumping forward by 10 changes only the tens digit: 7, 17, 27, 37.
Jumping back by 10: 86, 76, 66. The ones digit stays the same.

example.q: Start at 53. Jump back by 10 three times.

learn.reallife: When you get ₹10 pocket money every week, your savings go up by 10 each time: ₹15, ₹25, ₹35.

quiz.q: What is 34 + 6?
What is 42 − 15?
quiz.mistake: Takes the smaller ones digit from the bigger

quiz.q: Start at 95 and jump back by 10 two times. Where do you land?
When we jump forward or back by 10, which digit stays the same?
quiz.explain: Only the tens digit changes. 46, 56, 66 all end in 6.

quiz.q: Table: start 12, rule 'add 10, then add 10 again'. What is the result?
Start at 64. Jump back 10, then forward 1. Where are you?
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the order of jumps

quiz.q: On a bead string, Asha is at 58. She moves to 30. How many beads did she take away?

teach.ask: Gappu jumps by 10 from 3: 3, 13, 23. He asks why the 3 never changes. Can you explain?
teach.praise: Adding 10 adds one more ten, so the ones stay the same! Chirp!
teach.nudge: Which digit changes when I add 10?

learn.hook: On a 1-100 grid, one step down is +10. One step right is +1. Let us zoom around!
points: On a 1-100 grid, moving right adds 1 and moving left takes away 1.
Moving down a row adds 10 and moving up a row takes away 10.
45 + 34: go down 3 rows (75), then right 4 (79).
75 − 56: go up 5 rows (25), then left 6 (19).
Words for adding: more, added to, total, sum. Words for taking away: take away, difference, less, reduce.

example.q: How big is the jump from 23 to 34 on the grid?

learn.reallife: Seats in a cinema hall or a train coach are often numbered in rows and columns, like a grid.

quiz.q: On a 1-100 grid, what is 2 rows below 37?
What is 45 + 34? (Go down 3 rows, then right 4.)
What is 75 − 56? (Go up 5 rows, then left 6.)
How big is the jump from 23 to 34?
Mohan rolls 25 and moves forward from 31. Where does he land?
Which word means you should SUBTRACT?
quiz.explain: The difference between two numbers is found by taking away.

quiz.q: 'Reduce 64 by 20.' What do you get?
'Find the sum of 38 and 41.' What is it?

teach.ask: Gappu is on 42 on the grid and wants to add 23. Which way should he move?
teach.praise: Down 2 rows to 62, right 3 to 65! Chirp!
teach.nudge: Which way do I move to add tens?

learn.hook: In a magic square, every row, column and diagonal adds to 15. Is it really magic?
points: We can place numbers from 1 to 9 so that rows and columns add up to given totals.
In a 3 by 3 magic square with 1 to 9, every row, column and diagonal adds up to 15.
The middle box of this magic square is always 5.
To find a missing box, take the other two numbers in its line away from 15.

example.q: Row 1: 2, 7, ___. The row must add to 15. What is missing?

learn.reallife: Magic squares have been carved on old temple walls in India. A famous one is at a Jain temple in Khajuraho.

games.title: Magic square 2 7 6 / 9 5 1 / 4 3 8
items: The number 5 is in the centre.

quiz.q: Magic square row: 4, 3, ___ adds to 15. What is missing?
Which number is in the centre of the 1 to 9 magic square?
quiz.explain: 5 is in the middle, because 1 + 5 + 9 = 15 and 4 + 5 + 6 = 15.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the biggest number is in the middle

quiz.q: Diagonal: 6, 5, ___ adds to 15. What is missing?
Column: ___, 9, 4 adds to 15. What is missing?
Is 3, 5, 8 a correct line in a magic square of 15?
Place 1, 2, 3 in a row so that it adds to the given total 6. What is 1 + 2 + 3?
quiz.mistake: Writes the digits side by side

quiz.q: A row has 7 and 2. The total must be 13. What goes in the third box?
All numbers 1 to 9 are used once in a magic square. What do they add up to?
quiz.mistake: Gives the total of one row

teach.ask: Gappu found a magic square with one empty box: 9, 5, ___. How can he fill it?
teach.nudge: What should every line add up to?

learn.hook: Nani Maa's basket has 85 tomatoes and 67 potatoes. Will it be more than 100? Guess first!
points: On a number line: 25 + 30 = 55, then 55 + 6 = 61.
Finding the missing part of 100: 100 tomatoes and carrots, 58 are tomatoes, so 42 are carrots.
Estimate first: 85 + 67 is about 90 + 70 = 160, so it is more than 100.
learn.reallife: At the mandi, sellers add up how many kilos they have sold in a day.

quiz.q: What is 25 + 36?
What is 85 + 67?
A basket has 100 tomatoes and carrots. 58 are tomatoes. How many are carrots?
Without adding exactly, is 48 + 39 more or less than 100?
quiz.explain: 48 is about 50 and 39 is about 40. 50 + 40 = 90, less than 100.

quiz.q: Which is the best estimate for 62 + 29?
Nani Maa sold 46 mangoes in the morning and 38 in the evening. How many in all?
Riya has 73 beans and Rahul has 59. How many more does Riya have?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts the smaller ones digit from the bigger

quiz.q: Which sum is MORE than 100?

teach.ask: Gappu wants to add 47 + 38 but the ones make more than 10. What should he do?
teach.nudge: What do I do when the ones add up to more than 9?

learn.hook: A long box for the whole, two small boxes for the parts. Now any story sum is easy!
points: A box diagram has a big box for the whole (total) and smaller boxes for the parts.
If both parts are known, add them to find the whole.
If the whole and one part are known, subtract to find the other part.
You can make your own story from two numbers, like 35 and 20: 'Raju had 35 marbles and won 20 more.'

example.q: Whole = 64 vadas. Part 1 = 28 sold in the morning. Find Part 2.

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers think in parts and wholes: sold today and still in the shop add up to the stock.

games.title: What goes in the box?
pairs: Subtract to find the other part

quiz.q: A bookshop sold 34 books on Monday and 45 on Tuesday. What goes in the WHOLE box?
quiz.explain: Both parts are known, so add: 34 + 45 = 79.

quiz.q: A team scored 82 runs. Ravi scored 47. How many did the rest of the team score?
In a box diagram, the whole is 60 and one part is 25. Which sum finds the other part?
quiz.explain: Whole minus the known part gives the other part.
quiz.mistake: Adds the whole and the part

quiz.q: A cart had 75 vadas. 48 were sold. How many vadas are left?
Which story fits the box diagram: parts 30 and 15, whole unknown?
options: Raju had 30 sweets and ate 15. How many left?
Raju had 30 sweets and got 15 more. How many now?
quiz.explain: Both parts are given and we join them to find the whole.

quiz.q: Parts: 26 girls and 29 boys. What is the whole?
Whole 100 runs. Part 1 is 64. What is Part 2?
Meena wrote: 'I had 40 stickers and gave 15 to Sita.' Which question fits?
options: How many does Meena have left?
quiz.explain: Giving away means a part is removed, so we ask how many are left.

teach.ask: Gappu's story: 'I had 30 seeds and ate 12.' How should he draw the box diagram?
teach.praise: Whole 30, one part 12, other part 18! Chirp!
teach.nudge: Which number goes in the big box?

topics.title: Race to 100 and open number lines

learn.hook: Add any number from 1 to 10 each turn. Who will say 100 first?
points: In Race to 100, players take turns adding a number from 1 to 10 to a running total.
The player who reaches exactly 100 wins.
Think ahead: from 90 to 99, you can win in one turn. From 89, the other player cannot win next.
Estimate a sum before you add: 56 + 38 is about 60 + 40 = 100, so close to 100.
An open number line can start at any number. Draw jumps for each part you add.

example.q: Solve 67 + 25 on an open number line.

learn.reallife: Board games and cricket chases make us think: how many more runs to reach the target?

quiz.q: In Race to 100, the total is 93. What must you add to win?
quiz.mistake: Takes the ones digit as the answer

quiz.q: The total is 85. Can you win in one turn (add 1 to 10)?
quiz.explain: 100 − 85 = 15, but you can add at most 10.

quiz.q: The total is 79. You add 10. What is the new total?
If you leave the total at 89, the other player adds 1 to 10. What is the biggest they can reach?
quiz.explain: 89 + 10 = 99. They cannot reach 100, so you can win next turn!

quiz.q: Estimate: is 47 + 46 more or less than 100?
quiz.explain: 47 + 46 is about 50 + 50 = 100, but both were rounded up, so it is less. Exactly 93.

quiz.q: On an open number line, start at 58 and jump +30, then +4. Where do you land?
Solve 76 + 18 with jumps: 76 + 10 = 86, then 86 + ___ = 94.
Which sum is closest to 100?

teach.ask: Gappu's total is 91 in Race to 100. What should he add, and why?

learn.hook: Can you add 39 + 26 in your head, with no paper? Here are some magic tricks!
points: To add 9, add 10 and take away 1: 46 + 9 = 56 − 1 = 55.
Add tens by jumping: 43 + 30 = 73, just 3 jumps of ten.
learn.reallife: At the sabzi market, you can add prices in your head and know the total before the shopkeeper tells you!

quiz.q: What is 47 + 9? Try this: add 10, then take away 1.
quiz.mistake: Adds 10 but forgets to take away the extra 1

quiz.q: Nani Maa gave 20 sweets to Riya and 20 sweets to Arjun. How many sweets did she give in all?
Double 15 is 30. So what is 15 + 16?
quiz.explain: 16 is one more than 15, so 15 + 16 is one more than 30. That is 31.
quiz.mistake: Gives the double without adding the extra 1

quiz.q: Which way gives the correct answer to 29 + 14?
quiz.explain: 29 is 1 less than 30. So 30 + 14 = 44, then take away 1 to get 43.
quiz.mistake: Rounds 29 up to 30 but then adds the extra 1 instead of taking it away

quiz.q: Kabir had 63 stamps. His uncle gave him 30 more. How many stamps does he have now?
What is 8 + 6? Make a ten first: 8 + 2 + 4.
quiz.mistake: Loses count when breaking 6 into 2 and 4

quiz.q: What is 70 − 30?
quiz.explain: 7 tens take away 3 tens leaves 4 tens. That is 40.

quiz.q: Harpreet bought a book for ₹49 and a pen for ₹20. Think ₹50 + ₹20 − ₹1. What is the total?
quiz.explain: ₹50 + ₹20 = ₹70. The book was ₹1 less than ₹50, so take away 1: ₹69.
quiz.mistake: Rounds up to 50 but forgets to take away the extra 1

teach.ask: Gappu wants to add 39 + 15 in his head but has no paper. Teach him a trick!
teach.praise: 40 + 15 = 55, take away 1 is 54! I am a mental maths bird now!
teach.nudge: If I make 39 into 40, what must I do at the end?
